pageObservations.observations: Lecture 17 Cartesian Space Schemes title only.
Learning outcomes roadmap lists Cartesian interpolation, geometry issues, runtime IK, languages, dynamics and collision-free motion; no unique teaching.
Contents agenda mirrors roadmap, including programming problem; no distinct examinable claims.

Cartesian scheme specifies tool position/orientation versus time; joint-space tool path depends on robot kinematics. User can choose line, circle, sinusoid and other paths. XYZ diagram shows robot, green START pose, three yellow intermediate poses and red END with position and orientation labels; no numerical lengths.

Tool frame {T} relative to station {S}; this workflow plans Cartesian functions without IK, then computes joint angles at runtime path-update rate. IK costs computation. Functions are splined; linear/parabolic spline common. This is not a universal prohibition on offline IK.

Linear interpolation of position; angle-axis orientation transition. Linear region has constant velocity; blends accelerate/decelerate. Last bullet incorrectly claims LSPB velocity AND acceleration continuity: matched quadratic/linear joins can preserve position/velocity while acceleration generally jumps.

Six-by-one chi stacks three station-referenced position entries and orientation K. Slide labels K=ROT(unit-axis,angle), dimensionally ambiguous if ROT means a matrix. A rotation vector theta*k makes three orientation entries; not a unique global Euclidean orientation coordinate.

Axis-angle has integer 360-degree winding equivalence. Source proposes minimizing norm(K_B-K_A) and calls it smallest angular displacement. Valid unwrap intuition for same fixed axis, not a universal SO(3) geodesic rule for noncommuting axes; need relative orientation composition.

Annular workspace drawing: dashed red A-to-B chord passes inner hole despite endpoints within annulus. Joint-space motion may be feasible while Cartesian straight line fails. Workspace geometry, not simply timing, causes failure.

Singularity page shows several arm postures along dashed A-B tool line, rates can grow or exceed bounds near singularity and tracking may deviate. Time scaling can reduce joint-rate demand but changes intended temporal attributes. Direction matters, and exact singularity is not necessarily repaired by nonzero slowing.

Equal-link planar arm shown in two configurations reaching A/B; source says joint limits can prevent a same-branch continuous Cartesian transition. Endpoint IK existence alone does not establish path feasibility. Systems may detect and report before motion, not guarantee all paths.

Runtime path generator supplies theta, theta-dot, theta-double-dot at update rate. Joint functions directly evaluated without runtime IK in this workflow; Cartesian tool shape not explicitly controlled. Cubic theta=a0+a1*t+a2*t^2+a3*t^3 printed; derivatives follow algebraically.
At segment end recall new cubic coefficients and reset local t=0. For LSPB test current local time each update to choose linear versus blend portion.

Joint linear theta=theta_j+theta_dot_jk*t, derivative constant, second derivative0. Blend s=t-(t_j/2+t_jk), theta=theta_j+v*(t-s)+(a/2)s^2 is printed alongside theta_dot=v+a*s and theta_ddot=a. Since t-s is constant these are inconsistent: printed position derivative is a*s. Graphs show a straight line and rounded LSPB with blend boundaries t_b and t_f-t_b; no zero-acceleration-join guarantee.

Cartesian generator interpolates tool positions/orientations, then IK yields joints; direct tool-path control adds singularity/multiple-solution costs. Same scalar equations applied componentwise to Cartesian chi. Coordinated/common progress is needed for a translational straight line, not automatic for arbitrary independent component clocks.

Cartesian linear x=x_j+v*t, xdot=v, xddot0. Time is said both elapsed since via point and calculated at planning time: elapsed runtime time advances, planned durations/slopes do not. Same inconsistent blend expression as p518 but Cartesian x notation. Printed t_inb formula and derivative conflict observed directly.

Conversion chi to homogeneous transform, then theta=SOLVE(transform). Source G/S frame labels differ earlier T/S convention, so map direction must be explicit. Numerical backward differences: qdot(t)=[q(t)-q(t-dt)]/dt and qddot(t)=[qdot(t)-qdot(t-dt)]/dt. No supplied robot IK or guarantee branch continuity.

Robot language defines via points plus speed/smoothness; interpreter invokes path generator. Examples MOVE ARM TO C (joint-space), ... LINEARLY (Cartesian line), ... VIA B (intermediate B). Illustrative syntax, not universal controller standard. Complex paths assembled from simple segments.

Fixed maximum acceleration at blend points is a simplification. Actual feasible acceleration depends on manipulator dynamics and actuator limits; torque-speed curves rather than universally constant torque/acceleration. Diagram red piecewise path goes above then right of block, but its drawn geometry is not a dynamically certified full-link path.

Conservative acceleration bound can underuse available speed; more general task optimizes time along GIVEN spatial path using rigid-body dynamics and torque-speed characteristics, usually numerically. Green smooth depicted path over obstacle; different illustration does not mean timing-only optimization changes a fixed path.

Collision-free path connects initial/final configurations avoiding obstacles and respecting manipulator constraints. Ideally user goal only, system chooses path/via points. Search may occur in joint or Cartesian space. Red dashed path crosses blue block and collision is labeled at tool/block contact, unlike next page.

Planner needs manipulator, workspace and obstacle models. Free-space graph connectivity/search contrasted with artificial potential goal attraction/obstacle repulsion and local-minimum traps. Source says exponential with joint count, not supplied graph-node count; a joint grid offers m^n state-growth explanation. Green path goes around block and label says Collision Free; no proof of all-link clearance from only tool trace.

Worked planar Cartesian affine move from (0.700,0.200,0 degrees) to (0.300,-0.400,60 degrees), duration4s. Asked pose/velocity/acceleration at2s. This states no robot geometry or rest boundary conditions.

Affine component laws x1+(x2-x1)t/tf, y1+(y2-y1)t/tf, phi1+(phi2-phi1)t/tf. Printed x slope(0.300-0.700)/4=-0.100 and y(-0.400-0.200)/4=-0.150. Correct signs and units distinguish positions from rates.
Orientation rate(60-0)/4=15deg/s; x=.700-.100t, y=.200-.150t, phi=15t. Worked x(2)=.500 shown; source worked-answer exposure before independently recomputing Q046/Q047.
Worked y(2)=.200-.150*2=-.100; phi(2)=15*2=30degrees; full pose [.500,-.100,30degrees]. Answer visible; independently rederive from endpoints rather than claim a source-answer-blind solve.
Constant Cartesian rate vector[-.100,-.150,15deg/s], zero second derivatives stated specifically for linear region. Source does not supply startup/shutdown blends or joint rates.
Final answer repeats pose [.500,-.100,30degrees], rates[-.100,-.150,15degrees/s], accelerations[0,0,0] from529-531. Checked incremental difference: only consolidated presentation, no new derivation.

Programming prompt repeats endpoints/duration and adds update interval0.2s; compute all three component positions, velocities, accelerations and print complete interval values. No plot requirement or robot model.

Actual code imports numpy, tf4 dt.2, endpoints then t=np.arange(0,tf+dt,dt); vector affine x/y/phi, constant slope arrays via ones_like(t), acceleration arrays assigned zeros_like(t). No measurements, IK, dynamics, collision tests or plotting calls.

Header has10 columns t,x,y,phi,xdot,ydot,phidot,xddot,yddot,phiddot. Loop i in range(len(t)); adjacent f-strings print t and phi/phidot to1decimal, x/y/xdot/ydot3decimals, accelerations1decimal. No plotting code on continuation.

Readable table21 rows t0.0 to4.0 step.2, 10columns. x decrements.020, y decrements.030, phi increments3.0; xdot-.100, ydot-.150, phidot15.0, accelerations0.0 all rows. Row1.4 gives.560,-.010,21.0; row2.0.500,-.100,30.0; final.300,-.400,60.0. Previously inferred row/index answers independently before viewing table.

Three time graphs: x decreases.7→.3; y decreases.2→-.4 crossing between1.2 and1.4; orientation increases0→60 labeled theta(t), unlike phi code. Samples on straight traces; orientation is task variable, not proven joint angle.

Velocity graphs all horizontal: xdot-.100 with narrow negative y-axis about-.096 to-.104, ydot-.150 about-.145 to-.155, angular15.0 about14.5 to15.5. Axis range is not temporal fluctuation. Code has no plotting calls despite output heading.

All three acceleration traces lie at0 with symmetric small positive/negative ticks; zero arrays reflect prescribed affine interior, not rest boundary transitions or a physical robot dynamics solution.

XY diagram blue line from green start(.7,.2) to red end(.3,-.4); actual motion down-left. Small orientation arrows generally right/up with increasing angle, independent of translation tangent. Legend identifies trajectory/start/end, no obstacle/robot geometry or feasibility proof.

Summary repeats tool/station relation, interpolation, LSPB, singularity/workspace limits, language via-points, runtime IK, dynamics and collisions. Incremental check: no new concept; runtime IK sentence scoped to Cartesian scheme and smooth does not repair acceleration-continuity conflict.
Bibliography only: Craig2005 Introduction to robotics Mechanics and control3rd edition. Not counted as new examinable content.
Thank You closing only; no printed number visible, unlike prior numbered pages.
